lessons.title: Base64
lessons.definition: An encoding represents bytes as text using a public 64-symbol alphabet. It provides no secret-key protection.
lessons.tool: Python 3 base64 library. Ubuntu base64 provides an alternative.

steps.title: Inspect your input
steps.command: cat inputs/01_base64.txt
steps.explain: Read the supplied plain-text practice file. You may edit its message.
steps.expected: Base64 represents bytes as text.

steps.title: Encode your file
steps.command:
python3 labs/01_base64.py encode inputs/01_base64.txt work/base64.txt
cat work/base64.txt
steps.explain: encode converts source bytes into Base64 text. It does not encrypt them.
steps.expected: A Base64 string that differs from the original message.

steps.title: Decode your output
steps.command:
python3 labs/01_base64.py decode work/base64.txt work/base64_recovered.txt
cat work/base64_recovered.txt
steps.explain: decode reverses the Base64 representation. This is a separate command.
steps.expected: The original message returns.

steps.title: Verify and try the native tool
steps.command:
cmp inputs/01_base64.txt work/base64_recovered.txt
base64 --decode work/base64.txt > work/base64_native.txt
cmp inputs/01_base64.txt work/base64_native.txt
steps.explain: cmp prints nothing when files match. --decode is the Ubuntu base64 reversal flag.
steps.expected: Both comparisons are silent and return status 0.

lessons.check: Explain why no secret key was needed. Change the input and repeat both directions.

lessons.title: ROT32
lessons.definition: A rotation cipher substitutes letters using an alphabet and shift. Here ASCII letters rotate by 32 modulo 26, equivalent to ROT6. This definition preserves case, digits and punctuation.
lessons.tool: Python 3 byte translation. ROT32 here is explicitly a 26-letter Caesar rotation.

steps.title: Inspect and encode
steps.command:
cat inputs/02_rot32.txt
python3 labs/02_rot32.py encode inputs/02_rot32.txt work/rot32.txt
cat work/rot32.txt
steps.explain: The forward operation shifts each letter by +32, equivalent to +6.
steps.expected: SOC becomes YUI. Digits 123 remain unchanged.

steps.title: Reverse the rotation
steps.command:
python3 labs/02_rot32.py decode work/rot32.txt work/rot32_recovered.txt
cat work/rot32_recovered.txt
steps.explain: The reverse operation shifts by -32. Applying +32 twice would not reverse it.
steps.expected: The original sentence returns.

steps.title: Verify the recovered bytes
steps.command: cmp inputs/02_rot32.txt work/rot32_recovered.txt
steps.explain: The entire file, including case and punctuation, must match.
steps.expected: No output means a byte-for-byte match.

lessons.check: Predict one letter substitution and explain why 32 wraps to 6.

lessons.title: gzip
lessons.definition: gzip is a compression format. Compression reduces redundancy and decompression reconstructs the original bytes. No secret key is involved.
lessons.tool: Python 3 gzip library. The gzip CLI can also decompress this exercise.

steps.title: Compress your file
steps.command:
python3 labs/03_gzip.py compress inputs/03_gzip.txt work/message.gz
od -An -tx1 -N 3 work/message.gz
steps.explain: compress creates a gzip stream. od shows its first three bytes in hexadecimal.
steps.expected: Header bytes: 1f 8b 08.

steps.title: Decompress your file
steps.command:
python3 labs/03_gzip.py decompress work/message.gz work/gzip_recovered.txt
cat work/gzip_recovered.txt
steps.explain: decompress reverses compression, with a 4 MiB output limit in this lab.
steps.expected: The repeated source sentence returns.

steps.title: Verify and use the native tool
steps.command:
cmp inputs/03_gzip.txt work/gzip_recovered.txt
gzip -dc work/message.gz > work/gzip_native.txt
cmp inputs/03_gzip.txt work/gzip_native.txt
steps.explain: gzip -d decompresses and -c writes to stdout. Redirection saves it to a file.
steps.expected: Both recovered files match the original.

lessons.check: Explain why opaque compressed bytes do not prove encryption.

lessons.title: XOR-92
lessons.definition: XOR compares bits and returns 1 where they differ. Repeating XOR with the same byte key reverses it. A single repeated byte key is weak obfuscation, with 256 possibilities.
lessons.tool: Python 3 bytewise ^ operator. Key 92 is decimal and equals hexadecimal 0x5c.

steps.title: Apply XOR to your file
steps.command:
python3 labs/04_xor.py encode inputs/04_xor.txt work/xor.bin --key 92
od -An -tx1 -N 16 work/xor.bin
steps.explain: --key 92 supplies a decimal byte. Each input byte combines with that value.
steps.expected: The output bytes differ from the original text.

steps.title: Reverse XOR with the same key
steps.command:
python3 labs/04_xor.py decode work/xor.bin work/xor_recovered.txt --key 92
cat work/xor_recovered.txt
steps.explain: The ^ operation is identical in both directions. (P XOR K) XOR K equals P.
steps.expected: The original practice sentence returns.

steps.title: Compare correct and incorrect keys
steps.command:
cmp inputs/04_xor.txt work/xor_recovered.txt
python3 labs/04_xor.py decode work/xor.bin work/xor_wrong.txt --key 93
cmp inputs/04_xor.txt work/xor_wrong.txt
steps.explain: XOR has no authentication tag. A wrong key can still produce output, so compare bytes.
steps.expected: First comparison matches. Second reports a difference and status 1.

lessons.check: Explain why wrong-key XOR output can exist while AES-GCM rejects it.

lessons.title: AES-256-GCM
lessons.definition: AES means Advanced Encryption Standard. It is symmetric: the same secret key enables encryption and decryption. Galois/Counter Mode adds authentication. This lab uses a 32-byte key, fresh 12-byte nonce and authentication tag.
lessons.tool: Node.js built-in node:crypto library. No npm package is required.

steps.title: Generate your secret key
steps.command: node labs/05_aes.js keygen keys/practice_aes.key
steps.explain: keygen creates 32 random bytes. Run this once, then retain the key.
steps.expected: A teaching key at keys/practice_aes.key.

steps.title: Encrypt your practice file
steps.command:
node labs/05_aes.js encrypt inputs/05_aes.txt work/aes.json keys/practice_aes.key
cat work/aes.json
steps.explain: encrypt creates a fresh nonce and tag. Binary fields use Base64 for JSON storage.
steps.expected: A packet with algorithm, nonce_b64, tag_b64 and ciphertext_b64. It does not contain the key.

steps.title: Decrypt using your key
steps.command:
node labs/05_aes.js decrypt work/aes.json work/aes_recovered.txt keys/practice_aes.key
cat work/aes_recovered.txt
steps.explain: decrypt decodes the packet fields, uses the secret key, and verifies the GCM tag before writing output.
steps.expected: The original practice sentence returns.

steps.title: Verify, then test a wrong key
steps.command:
cmp inputs/05_aes.txt work/aes_recovered.txt
node labs/05_aes.js keygen keys/wrong_aes.key
node labs/05_aes.js decrypt work/aes.json work/aes_wrong.txt keys/wrong_aes.key
steps.explain: Use a different generated key. The final command must fail authentication.
steps.expected: Comparison matches. Wrong-key command exits nonzero and writes no new plaintext file.

lessons.check: Identify the key, nonce, ciphertext and tag. Explain why Base64 decoding alone cannot recover the message.

lessons.title: RSA-OAEP
lessons.definition: RSA, named for Rivest, Shamir and Adleman, is asymmetric. For confidentiality, the public key encrypts and the matching private key decrypts. OAEP is Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding. This lab uses RSA-2048 and SHA-256.
lessons.tool: Node.js built-in node:crypto library. RSA here protects short messages or AES keys.

steps.title: Generate your key pair
steps.command: node labs/06_rsa.js keygen keys/practice_rsa
steps.explain: keygen creates a public PEM and a private PEM. Retain the matching pair.
steps.expected: keys/practice_rsa.public.pem and keys/practice_rsa.private.pem.

steps.title: Encrypt your short message
steps.command:
node labs/06_rsa.js encrypt inputs/06_rsa.txt work/rsa.b64 keys/practice_rsa.public.pem
cat work/rsa.b64
steps.explain: The public key encrypts the input using OAEP-SHA256. Output uses Base64.
steps.expected: A Base64 representation of RSA ciphertext. Values vary each run.

steps.title: Decrypt with the private key
steps.command:
node labs/06_rsa.js decrypt work/rsa.b64 work/rsa_recovered.txt keys/practice_rsa.private.pem
cat work/rsa_recovered.txt
steps.explain: The matching private key reverses RSA encryption using the same OAEP parameters.
steps.expected: The short practice message returns.

steps.title: Verify the recovered message
steps.command: cmp inputs/06_rsa.txt work/rsa_recovered.txt
steps.explain: A Base64-wrapped public key is still a public key. Decoding it does not create a private key.
steps.expected: No output means success. This RSA configuration accepts at most 190 input bytes.

lessons.check: Explain why RSA wraps the 32-byte AES key in the capstone instead of the entire payload.

cap_build.title: Create your capstone working folder
cap_build.explain: The payload is harmless JavaScript source. Keep it as data during analysis.
cap_build.expected: A trainingEvent object and console print.

cap_build.title: Apply rotation and XOR
cap_build.command:
python3 labs/02_rot32.py encode inputs/capstone_payload.js work/create/rotated.txt
python3 labs/04_xor.py encode work/create/rotated.txt work/create/xor.bin --key 92
cap_build.explain: Apply two routines you practiced. The sequence matters.
cap_build.expected: Rotated text, followed by XOR ciphertext bytes.

cap_build.title: Compress and AES-encrypt
cap_build.command:
python3 labs/03_gzip.py compress work/create/xor.bin work/create/payload.gz
node labs/05_aes.js keygen keys/student_capstone.key
node labs/05_aes.js encrypt work/create/payload.gz work/create/aes.json keys/student_capstone.key
cap_build.explain: Compress the XOR bytes, then protect them using your own AES key.
cap_build.expected: A gzip file and an authenticated AES packet.

cap_build.title: Wrap the AES key with RSA
cap_build.command:
node labs/06_rsa.js keygen keys/student_capstone
node labs/06_rsa.js encrypt keys/student_capstone.key work/create/wrapped_key.b64 keys/student_capstone.public.pem
cap_build.explain: Hybrid encryption: RSA protects the short AES key. AES protects the full data.
cap_build.expected: RSA ciphertext containing the encrypted AES key.

cap_build.title: Package and Base64-encode one final file
cap_build.command:
python3 exercises/capstone.py package --directory work/create --envelope work/create/envelope.json
python3 labs/01_base64.py encode work/create/envelope.json work/create/my_capstone.b64
cap_build.explain: package only combines existing fields. Base64 creates the final text artifact.

cap_recover.title: Decode the supplied final file
cap_recover.command:
mkdir -p work/capstone
python3 labs/01_base64.py decode challenges/all_layers.b64 work/capstone/envelope.json
cat work/capstone/envelope.json
cap_recover.explain: Base64 is the outside representation of a packet carrying encrypted data and an RSA-wrapped AES key.
cap_recover.expected: A JSON envelope with wrapped_key_b64 and aes_packet.

cap_recover.title: Extract the two encrypted fields
cap_recover.explain: This helper separates fields into files. It performs no decryption.

cap_recover.title: Recover the AES key with RSA
cap_recover.command: node labs/06_rsa.js decrypt work/capstone/wrapped_key.b64 work/capstone/aes.key keys/capstone.private.pem
cap_recover.explain: Use the supplied matching private key. The output is a binary AES key.
cap_recover.expected: A 32-byte key. Check with: wc -c work/capstone/aes.key

cap_recover.title: Decrypt AES, then decompress gzip
cap_recover.command:
node labs/05_aes.js decrypt work/capstone/aes.json work/capstone/payload.gz work/capstone/aes.key
python3 labs/03_gzip.py decompress work/capstone/payload.gz work/capstone/xor.bin
cap_recover.explain: Verify AES-GCM authentication before saving gzip bytes, then decompress.
cap_recover.expected: XOR ciphertext bytes remain after decompression.

cap_recover.title: Reverse XOR and the rotation
cap_recover.command:
python3 labs/04_xor.py decode work/capstone/xor.bin work/capstone/rotated.txt --key 92
python3 labs/02_rot32.py decode work/capstone/rotated.txt work/capstone/recovered.js
cap_recover.explain: Reverse the inner transformations in the opposite order from construction.
cap_recover.expected: Readable harmless JavaScript source, without executing it.

cap_recover.title: Inspect and verify the payload
cap_recover.explain: Compare exact bytes to the original. A URL string alone does not show a network action.

incident.title: Inspect and preserve the supplied case
incident.command:
cat challenges/incident/READ_ME_TRAINING.txt
cat challenges/incident/events.csv
sha256sum challenges/incident/bundle.lab.b64
incident.explain: All events are synthetic. Record source evidence before recovery.
incident.expected: Three synthetic encrypted-copy events and a training note.

incident.title: Decode the evidence bundle
incident.command:
mkdir -p work/incident/recovered
python3 labs/01_base64.py decode challenges/incident/bundle.lab.b64 work/incident/bundle.json
python3 exercises/incident.py extract
incident.explain: Decode Base64 and split the three records. No decryption happens in extract.
incident.expected: Three AES packets and three RSA-wrapped keys under work/incident.

incident.title: Recover the first document key
incident.command: node labs/06_rsa.js decrypt work/incident/invoice.txt.wrapped.b64 work/incident/invoice.key keys/incident.private.pem
incident.explain: The incident private key is supplied by the instructor for this exercise.
incident.expected: A recovered 32-byte AES key for invoice.txt.

incident.title: Restore the first document
incident.command:
node labs/05_aes.js decrypt work/incident/invoice.txt.aes.json work/incident/recovered/invoice.txt work/incident/invoice.key
cat work/incident/recovered/invoice.txt
incident.explain: Use the recovered file key to authenticate and decrypt the invoice packet.

incident.title: Restore the remaining documents
incident.command:
for name in staff.csv recovery-plan.txt; do
  node labs/06_rsa.js decrypt "work/incident/$name.wrapped.b64" "work/incident/$name.key" keys/incident.private.pem
  node labs/05_aes.js decrypt "work/incident/$name.aes.json" "work/incident/recovered/$name" "work/incident/$name.key"
done
incident.explain: Apply the same recovery workflow to the remaining fixed training records.
incident.expected: staff.csv and recovery-plan.txt appear in the recovered directory.

incident.title: Validate and report recovery
incident.explain: The verifier compares each recovered document’s SHA-256 to a known-good baseline.
incident.expected: Three PASS lines, one for each document.
